Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI30 · Fuzzy logic and vague categories

AI20 · Local optimization and evolutionary search

AI33 · Reinforcement learning

AI34 · Neural networks and deep learning

Correct answer: B — Fuzzy logic

Fuzzy logic represents imprecise categories through graded membership, so an input can belong to a category to a degree rather than only completely or not at all. This differs from uncertainty about whether an event occurs. Genetic search, neural networks and reinforcement learning can be combined with fuzzy methods, but their defining mechanisms do not supply this membership interpretation.

Evidence in the complete study note

Fuzzy sets assign graded membership μ(x) between 0 and 1 to concepts such as warm or tall. A temperature can belong to warm with degree 0.7. This is not a 70% probability that an otherwise crisp warm proposition is true. Boolean logic uses only true and false; probability describes uncertainty about events.AI30
A genetic algorithm maintains a population, evaluates fitness, selects parents, applies crossover and mutation, and repeats replacement. It searches without guaranteeing global optimality. Means–ends analysis selects a difference between current and goal states, chooses an operator reducing it, and recursively solves its preconditions. Neither method is simply A* running backward.AI20
An RL agent observes state information, takes an action, receives reward and a new observation, and improves its policy to maximize expected cumulative reward. Rewards evaluate outcomes rather than supply the correct action label. Rewards may be delayed; not every correct-looking action receives immediate reward.AI33
Training adjusts weights, often through gradients and backpropagation.AI34

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Genetic algorithms evolve populations; graded category membership is not their defining mechanism.

B · correct — Fuzzy logic represents degrees of membership in vague categories.

C · incorrect — Neural networks adjust weighted representations and do not inherently define fuzzy membership.

D · incorrect — Reinforcement learning uses rewards and policy improvement rather than defining graded category membership.

A genetic algorithm maintains a population, evaluates fitness, selects parents, applies crossover and mutation, and repeats replacement. It searches without guaranteeing global optimality. The module lists simple reflex, model-based reflex, goal-based, utility-based and learning agents (PDF pp. 14–15). “Unity-based” is not “utility-based” and is not one of those classes.

The common teaching list contains five agent classes when learning agents are included, or four decision architectures before learning is added. State the convention when counting agent types. “Target-based” can mean goal-based; “unity-based” is not utility-based.AI42
A simple reflex agent matches condition–action rules against the current percept only: if dirty, clean. It has no persistent world-state memory. This is adequate when the current observation contains everything needed for its rule, but partial observability can make the same percept require different actions.AI06
The performance element selects actions. The learning element changes the agent to improve future performance. The critic evaluates behavior against a performance standard and supplies feedback. The problem generator suggests exploratory actions likely to yield useful experience.AI08

Question 75

Which agent architecture applies fixed condition–action rules directly to the current percept, without retaining an internal world-state model?

  • A. Simple reflex agent
  • B. Model-based agent
  • C. Goal-based agent
  • D. Utility-based agent

Adapted from

  • Artificial Intelligence practice questions · Question 27

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Read the relevant agent component, action-selection criterion or environment dimension. Use only properties established by the description.

Study-guide sections

AI06 · Simple and model-based reflex agents

AI07 · Goals, utility and model updates

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI06 · Simple and model-based reflex agents

AI07 · Goals, utility and model updates

Correct answer: A — Simple reflex agent

The absence of persistent internal state is the key distinction. A simple reflex agent maps the current percept to an action using condition–action rules. Model-based reflex agents may also use rules, but they maintain a world-state representation. Goal-based and utility-based agents use goals or outcome preferences to guide selection, rather than being defined by current-percept-only rule matching.

Evidence in the complete study note

A simple reflex agent matches condition–action rules against the current percept only: if dirty, clean. It has no persistent world-state memory. This is adequate when the current observation contains everything needed for its rule, but partial observability can make the same percept require different actions.AI06
A model-based reflex agent maintains internal state using the previous state, previous action, current percept, and models of world change and action effects. It then applies rules to that state. Both kinds can use condition–action rules; memory and a world model distinguish them.AI06
A goal-based agent considers future action sequences that reach a desired state. A utility-based agent compares degrees of desirability and trade-offs, choosing maximum expected utility: EU(a)=Σs P(s|a,evidence)U(s). Reaching the destination is a goal; balancing arrival time, safety and cost requires preferences among outcomes.AI07

Choice by choice

A · correct — A simple reflex agent chooses from the current percept without persistent world-state memory.

B · incorrect — A model-based reflex agent adds internal state and applies rules to that modeled state.

C · incorrect — Goal-based selection evaluates actions or future sequences against a desired state.

D · incorrect — Utility-based selection ranks outcomes by desirability or expected utility.

Question 80

A face-recognition system is built to control entry to a building, without trying to explain biological recognition processes. Which approach classifies this practical engineering purpose, rather than its breadth of capability?

  • A. Weak AI approach
  • B. Applied AI approach
  • C. Cognitive AI approach
  • D. Strong AI approach

Adapted from

  • Artificial Intelligence practice questions · Question 32

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Read the definition and the classification axis requested; distinguish the defining purpose from supporting techniques or implementation resources.

Study-guide sections

AI01 · AI capabilities and scope

AI43 · Clarify overlapping learning and AI labels

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI01 · AI capabilities and scope

AI43 · Clarify overlapping learning and AI labels

Correct answer: B — Applied AI approach

Applied AI builds useful solutions to practical tasks, so building-access recognition fits that purpose. The same system is also narrow or weak AI in capability scope. These labels answer different classification questions and are compatible. Cognitive AI would investigate biological intelligence, while strong-AI claims concern broader competence or actual understanding. The explicit purpose axis isolates the intended selection.

Evidence in the complete study note

Artificial intelligence studies systems that perform tasks requiring intelligence: reasoning, learning, planning, perception and language. Applied AI builds useful solutions; cognitive AI uses computational models to investigate biological intelligence. A model should be compared with human behavior or experimental observations before claiming it explains human thought.AI01
Narrow or weak AI addresses bounded tasks, such as face recognition, spam filtering or a voice assistant. General AI denotes broad competence transferable across domains; strong AI also has a philosophical meaning involving actual understanding. Do not equate a humanoid body, autonomous vehicle, or many features with general intelligence.AI01
Face recognition is both an applied task and a narrow capability. Broad machine-intelligence goals can include emulating human intelligence and building systems that learn. Humanlike problem-solving alone does not uniquely select expert systems. Python is widely used, but C++ and Java also implement AI; “commonly used” does not isolate one language. McCarthy is associated with naming AI, not its sole invention.AI43

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Weak AI describes bounded capability, which also fits face recognition, but does not classify the purpose requested.

B · correct — Applied AI builds a useful practical solution, matching the entry-control purpose.

C · incorrect — Cognitive AI investigates biological intelligence; that is not the stated purpose.

D · incorrect — Strong AI concerns actual understanding or broad intelligence claims, not the application purpose described.

Question 86

What is the name of Artificial Intelligence which allows machines to handle vague information with a deftness that mimics human intuition?

  • A. Human intelligence
  • B. Boolean logic
  • C. Functional logic
  • D. Fuzzy logic

Source

  • Artificial Intelligence practice questions · Question 38

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Translate the statement carefully, then check the scope of its quantifiers, connectives or inference rule. Distinguish guaranteed consequences from plausible generalizations or explanations.

Study-guide sections

AI30 · Fuzzy logic and vague categories

AI25 · Propositional logic and models

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI30 · Fuzzy logic and vague categories

AI25 · Propositional logic and models

Correct answer: D — Fuzzy logic.

AI30 represents vague categories with degrees between zero and one and explains fuzzy control using graded rules. This supplies the concrete mechanism behind the stem’s loose phrase about human intuition. Boolean logic uses only true or false. Human intelligence is not the named machine-reasoning formalism here, and functional logic is not the provided graded-membership method.

Evidence in the complete study note

Fuzzy sets assign graded membership μ(x) between 0 and 1 to concepts such as warm or tall. A temperature can belong to warm with degree 0.7. This is not a 70% probability that an otherwise crisp warm proposition is true. Boolean logic uses only true and false; probability describes uncertainty about events.AI30
Propositional atoms represent whole true-or-false claims. ¬P negates; P∧Q requires both; P∨Q requires at least one; P→Q is false only when P is true and Q false; P↔Q requires matching truth values. Thus P→Q ≡ ¬P∨Q. De Morgan gives ¬(P∧Q) ≡ ¬P∨¬Q.AI25

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Human intelligence names biological capability, not the specified artificial graded-membership technique.

B · incorrect — Boolean logic uses crisp true/false values rather than degrees of membership in vague categories.

C · incorrect — Functional logic is not the graded-membership and fuzzy-rule formalism described in AI30.

D · correct — Fuzzy logic handles vague linguistic categories through graded membership and graded rules.

  • B. Utility based

  • D. Search frontier

AI42 · Distinguish agent categories and components

AI07 · Goals, utility and model updates

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI42 · Distinguish agent categories and components

AI12 · Frontiers and evaluation criteria

AI06 · Simple and model-based reflex agents

AI07 · Goals, utility and model updates

Correct answer: D — Search frontier

Model-based, utility-based and simple reflex describe ways to organize agent decision making. A search frontier instead stores generated nodes awaiting selection or expansion during a search. It is an algorithm component rather than a decision architecture. The overlapping target-based distractor has been replaced because target-based can reasonably mean goal-based, which is a valid agent category.

Evidence in the complete study note

The common teaching list contains five agent classes when learning agents are included, or four decision architectures before learning is added. State the convention when counting agent types. “Target-based” can mean goal-based; “unity-based” is not utility-based.AI42
A search node records a state plus parent, action, depth and path cost. Expanding a node generates its successors. OPEN or frontier stores discovered candidates awaiting expansion; CLOSED records expanded states. Reaching the same state through different paths does not imply the same node or cost.AI12
A simple reflex agent matches condition–action rules against the current percept only: if dirty, clean.AI06
A model-based reflex agent maintains internal state using the previous state, previous action, current percept, and models of world change and action effects.AI06
A goal-based agent considers future action sequences that reach a desired state. A utility-based agent compares degrees of desirability and trade-offs, choosing maximum expected utility: EU(a)=Σs P(s|a,evidence)U(s). Reaching the destination is a goal; balancing arrival time, safety and cost requires preferences among outcomes.AI07

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — A model-based architecture maintains an internal representation used in action selection.

B · incorrect — A utility-based architecture selects using outcome desirability.

C · incorrect — Simple reflex is a current-percept condition–action architecture.

D · correct — A search frontier is the collection of generated candidates awaiting selection, not an agent decision architecture.

Question 98

Which learning regime improves an agent’s action choices through interaction with an environment that supplies rewards or penalties?

  • A. Supervised learning
  • B. Reinforcement learning
  • C. Semi-supervised learning
  • D. Unsupervised learning

Study-guide sections

AI33 · Reinforcement learning

AI32 · Unsupervised, semi-supervised and active learning

AI31 · Supervised learning and prediction

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI33 · Reinforcement learning

AI32 · Unsupervised, semi-supervised and active learning

AI31 · Supervised learning and prediction

Correct answer: B — Reinforcement learning

Interaction alone is too broad to identify a learning regime. Here the environment supplies rewards or penalties for the agent’s actions, and the agent improves its choices from that feedback. This defines reinforcement learning. Supervised and semi-supervised methods depend on target labels; unsupervised methods discover unlabeled structure. None of those label-based descriptions specifies this action-and-reward loop.

Evidence in the complete study note

An RL agent observes state information, takes an action, receives reward and a new observation, and improves its policy to maximize expected cumulative reward. Rewards evaluate outcomes rather than supply the correct action label. Rewards may be delayed; not every correct-looking action receives immediate reward.AI33
Semi-supervised learning combines some labels with additional unlabeled data. Active learning chooses informative cases for an oracle to label; it still uses labels. “Exploratory learning” is not an exclusive standard synonym: it can mean unsupervised exploration or active data acquisition, so define the feedback. A task named summarization or time-series analysis is not automatically supervised; its training targets determine that.AI32
Supervised learning fits a mapping from labeled input–target examples.AI31
Unsupervised learning seeks structure without target labels: clustering groups similar examples; association finds co-occurrence; dimensionality reduction compresses features.AI32

Choice by choice

B · correct — Reinforcement learning improves decisions through environmental reward feedback.

C · incorrect — Semi-supervised learning mixes labeled and unlabeled examples, not a defining action-reward objective.

D · incorrect — Unsupervised learning seeks unlabeled structure without the stated reward-feedback objective.

Question 102

For DFS on an implicit tree with branching factor b and maximum depth m, storing pending siblings, which expression gives the standard worst-case space bound?

  • A. b
  • B. b^2
  • C. b^b
  • D. O(bm)

Adapted from

  • Artificial Intelligence practice questions · Question 54

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Check how the method selects its next candidate, what information it uses, and which cost, depth or heuristic assumptions the question supplies.

Study-guide sections

AI14 · Depth-first search

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI14 · Depth-first search

Correct answer: D — O(bm)

Depth-first search retains the active branch and pending alternatives rather than an entire breadth frontier. With up to b pending entries per level over depth m, the standard stored-frontier space bound is O(bm). Path-only on-demand generation can use O(m), but that is a different implementation convention. The expression gives the depth-dependent storage bound rather than an exponential time bound.

Evidence in the complete study note

DFS follows the deepest pending branch using a LIFO stack or recursion. FILO means the same order as LIFO. With the same children as BFS, a left-first DFS visits S,A,C before B; push rightmost children first to pop the leftmost first.AI14
Implicit-tree worst-case time is O(b^m), and space is O(bm) when pending siblings are stored, or O(m) for path-only recursive generation. DFS is not generally optimal and can fail on infinite paths or cycles. On a finite graph, visited-state tracking makes traversal complete but needs O(V) storage. Do not confuse the O(b^m) worst-case time bound with the DFS space bounds above.AI14

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — b omits growth with search depth m in the general DFS storage bound.

B · incorrect — b² is not the stated depth-dependent worst-case DFS storage expression.

C · incorrect — b^b is neither of the note’s DFS space bounds.

D · correct — With pending siblings, at most a branching-factor-sized set per depth gives the standard O(bm) space bound.

Question 103

For BFS on an implicit tree with branching factor b>1 and shallowest goal depth d, using generation-time goal testing, which expression gives the standard worst-case generated-node order?

  • A. b
  • B. b^d
  • C. b^2
  • D. b^b

Adapted from

  • Artificial Intelligence practice questions · Question 55

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Check how the method selects its next candidate, what information it uses, and which cost, depth or heuristic assumptions the question supplies.

Study-guide sections

AI13 · Breadth-first search

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI13 · Breadth-first search

Correct answer: B — b^d

BFS generates levels in order. Under generation-time goal testing, the generated nodes through the shallowest goal depth d are bounded by the geometric sum 1+b+…+b^d, whose dominant term is b^d when b>1. Testing only after expanding deeper nodes can change the conventional bound by another factor of b, so the question states the goal-test convention.

Evidence in the complete study note

The tree contains 1+b+…+b^d nodes through depth d, giving O(b^d) under generation-time goal testing. Expanding depth-d nodes before testing can generate depth d+1 and yields O(b^(d+1)); specify the convention. Explicit finite graph traversal with visited-state tracking takes O(V+E) time and O(V) space.AI13

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — b counts one level and does not account for arbitrary goal depth.

B · correct — The sum 1+b+…+b^d has order b^d for b>1.

C · incorrect — b² only describes a fixed depth-two case rather than general depth d.

D · incorrect — b^b wrongly replaces solution depth d with the branching factor.

Question 104

Which labels describe the recursive DFS stack’s removal order? Select all that apply.

  • A. LIFO
  • B. LILO
  • C. FIFO
  • D. FILO

Adapted from

  • Artificial Intelligence practice questions · Question 56

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Check how the method selects its next candidate, what information it uses, and which cost, depth or heuristic assumptions the question supplies.

Study-guide sections

AI14 · Depth-first search

AI13 · Breadth-first search

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI14 · Depth-first search

AI13 · Breadth-first search

Correct answers (select all): A, D — LIFO; FILO

Recursive depth-first search returns first from the most recently entered unfinished call. That is last-in-first-out stack order, also called first-in-last-out. The two labels are synonyms rather than distinct data structures. FIFO or LILO describes the opposite end-to-end order and does not characterize the DFS call stack. The multiple-selection instruction therefore retains both correct names for the same discipline.

Evidence in the complete study note

DFS follows the deepest pending branch using a LIFO stack or recursion. FILO means the same order as LIFO. With the same children as BFS, a left-first DFS visits S,A,C before B; push rightmost children first to pop the leftmost first.AI14
BFS removes the oldest frontier entry using a FIFO queue. Start with the root, remove the head, test it, append unseen successors at the tail, and repeat. It explores depths 0,1,2,… and is complete for finite b and a finite-depth goal. It minimizes number of edges, so minimum cost requires equal positive step costs.AI13

Choice by choice

A · correct — LIFO is the stack order used by recursion and depth-first exploration.

B · incorrect — LILO does not express the required last-in-first-out removal order.

C · incorrect — FIFO is queue order, associated with breadth-first rather than depth-first selection.

D · correct — FILO is another name for LIFO and therefore also describes the DFS stack.

AI15 · Uniform-cost search and Dijkstra

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI16 · Depth limits, iterative deepening and two directions

AI15 · Uniform-cost search and Dijkstra

Correct answer: C — Bidirectional Search

The algorithm starts one search at the initial state and another at the goal and stops at their intersection. Evidence: PDF 23.

Evidence in the complete study note

Bidirectional search grows from start and goal until frontiers connect. With suitable reverse actions, meeting tests and equal-cost BFS, time and space may fall to O(b^(d/2)). Weighted variants require a sound stopping bound; the first intersection need not be cheapest. IDA* deepens an f=g+h threshold rather than only a depth limit.AI16
UCS uses a priority queue ordered by actual accumulated path cost g(n). Remove a minimum-g node; accept a goal when removed, not when first generated. Relax each edge: if a cheaper path is found, update its frontier cost and parent.AI15
DLS runs DFS to depth ℓ and reports cutoff separately from failure. It misses goals deeper than ℓ. Iterative deepening runs DLS with limits 0,1,2,…; for finite b it finds the shallowest solution with O(b^d) time and O(bd) frontier space, optimal for equal step costs. Repeated shallow work is small compared with the deepest level.AI16

B · incorrect — Repeats depth-limited search from the start. See PDF p. 23.

C · correct — Exactly the two-front definition. See PDF p. 23.

D · incorrect — C explicitly fits. See PDF p. 23.

AI17 · Heuristics and greedy best-first search

Correct answer: C — f(n) = h(n)

AI13 · Breadth-first search

AI14 · Depth-first search

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI17 · Heuristics and greedy best-first search

AI13 · Breadth-first search

AI14 · Depth-first search

Correct answers (select all): C, D — The one closest to the goal node; Minimum heuristic cost

Greedy best-first search orders the frontier by h alone, choosing the smallest estimated remaining cost and ignoring cost already paid. Under the explicit interpretation, estimated closest to the goal and minimum heuristic cost express that same rule. Shallowest-first uses depth as in breadth-first search, while deepest-first follows depth-first ordering. Both heuristic descriptions are therefore valid and neither depth description is selected.

Evidence in the complete study note

Best-first is a family that orders OPEN by an evaluation function. Greedy best-first uses f=h and removes the smallest estimate, ignoring the cost already paid. It can choose an expensive route, loop without duplicate checks, or follow an infinite misleading branch. On a finite graph with full duplicate handling it is complete, but not generally optimal. Its implicit finite-tree worst case can be O(b^m).AI17
BFS removes the oldest frontier entry using a FIFO queue. Start with the root, remove the head, test it, append unseen successors at the tail, and repeat. It explores depths 0,1,2,… and is complete for finite b and a finite-depth goal. It minimizes number of edges, so minimum cost requires equal positive step costs.AI13
DFS follows the deepest pending branch using a LIFO stack or recursion. FILO means the same order as LIFO. With the same children as BFS, a left-first DFS visits S,A,C before B; push rightmost children first to pop the leftmost first.AI14

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Shallowest-first is BFS-style depth ordering rather than greedy heuristic selection.

B · incorrect — Deepest-first is DFS-style selection rather than minimum estimated remaining cost.

C · correct — Read closest as estimated by h; it is the same greedy criterion as minimum heuristic cost.

D · correct — Greedy best-first selects a node with minimum h, ignoring already-paid path cost.

Which general search family contains A* because it selects frontier nodes by a minimum evaluation value?

  • A. Breadth-First-Search
  • B. Depth-First-Search
  • C. Uniform Cost Search
  • D. Best-First-Search

Study-guide sections

AI18 · Admissibility, consistency and A*

AI15 · Uniform-cost search and Dijkstra

AI17 · Heuristics and greedy best-first search

AI13 · Breadth-first search

AI14 · Depth-first search

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI18 · Admissibility, consistency and A*

AI15 · Uniform-cost search and Dijkstra

AI17 · Heuristics and greedy best-first search

AI13 · Breadth-first search

AI14 · Depth-first search

Correct answer: D — Best-First-Search

Best-first search is the general family that selects a frontier node according to an evaluation value. A* is one member, using f=g+h. Uniform-cost search is another member, using g alone. Breadth-first and depth-first names describe depth-oriented selection disciplines. The question asks for the containing family rather than claiming A* is identical to one simpler algorithm.

Evidence in the complete study note

A* orders by f(n)=g(n)+h(n). Admissibility means 0≤h(n)≤h*(n), the true cheapest remaining cost. Consistency means h(n)≤c(n,n′)+h(n′) on every edge, with h(goal)=0; it implies admissibility on states with goal paths. Consistency makes f nondecreasing along a path.AI18
UCS uses a priority queue ordered by actual accumulated path cost g(n). Remove a minimum-g node; accept a goal when removed, not when first generated. Relax each edge: if a cheaper path is found, update its frontier cost and parent.AI15
Best-first is a family that orders OPEN by an evaluation function. Greedy best-first uses f=h and removes the smallest estimate, ignoring the cost already paid. It can choose an expensive route, loop without duplicate checks, or follow an infinite misleading branch. On a finite graph with full duplicate handling it is complete, but not generally optimal. Its implicit finite-tree worst case can be O(b^m).AI17
BFS removes the oldest frontier entry using a FIFO queue.AI13
DFS follows the deepest pending branch using a LIFO stack or recursion.AI14

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — BFS selects by depth/FIFO order rather than the general evaluation-priority family.

B · incorrect — DFS follows stack/deepest-branch order rather than minimum evaluation priority.

C · incorrect — UCS is another best-first method using g alone; it is not the general family containing A*.

D · correct — Best-first search is the family that selects by an evaluation, with A* using g+h.

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI07 · Goals, utility and model updates

AI06 · Simple and model-based reflex agents

Correct answer: B — Update the state information to be like the one after executing the best action chosen

The final update uses the chosen action to predict what the agent’s internal state representation should look like after that action. It is distinct from the earlier update using the current percept. Updating memory does not execute an actuator or directly modify the external environment. Naming the exact instruction resolves the missing referent while preserving the model-update interpretation of the original prototype.

Evidence in the complete study note

Updating an internal state after selecting an action predicts the action’s effect; it does not itself modify the external environment. A stored variable named goal is insufficient to prove a goal-based policy if BEST_ACTION never uses it. Model-based, goal-based, utility-based and learning capabilities can coexist.AI07
A model-based reflex agent maintains internal state using the previous state, previous action, current percept, and models of world change and action effects. It then applies rules to that state. Both kinds can use condition–action rules; memory and a world model distinguish them.AI06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Updating an internal state representation does not itself modify the external environment.

B · correct — The final call predicts and records the internal state after the selected action.

C · incorrect — Neither internal update executes an environmental action or produces the next percept.

D · incorrect — Selecting an action and updating memory are distinct from changing the external world through execution.

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI17 · Heuristics and greedy best-first search

AI15 · Uniform-cost search and Dijkstra

AI13 · Breadth-first search

AI14 · Depth-first search

Correct answer: D — Insert newly generated nodes in the open list according to their evaluation function (lowest values first)

Greedy best-first search orders its frontier by h alone, the estimate of remaining cost. A priority-ordered OPEN list with the smallest evaluation first therefore implements the rule when that evaluation is h. Ordering by g would instead implement uniform-cost search. Unconditionally prepending or appending nodes gives stack-like or FIFO behavior without the required heuristic ranking.

Evidence in the complete study note

Best-first is a family that orders OPEN by an evaluation function. Greedy best-first uses f=h and removes the smallest estimate, ignoring the cost already paid. It can choose an expensive route, loop without duplicate checks, or follow an infinite misleading branch. On a finite graph with full duplicate handling it is complete, but not generally optimal. Its implicit finite-tree worst case can be O(b^m).AI17
UCS uses a priority queue ordered by actual accumulated path cost g(n). Remove a minimum-g node; accept a goal when removed, not when first generated. Relax each edge: if a cheaper path is found, update its frontier cost and parent.AI15
BFS removes the oldest frontier entry using a FIFO queue. Start with the root, remove the head, test it, append unseen successors at the tail, and repeat. It explores depths 0,1,2,… and is complete for finite b and a finite-depth goal. It minimizes number of edges, so minimum cost requires equal positive step costs.AI13
DFS follows the deepest pending branch using a LIFO stack or recursion. FILO means the same order as LIFO. With the same children as BFS, a left-first DFS visits S,A,C before B; push rightmost children first to pop the leftmost first.AI14

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Prepending every new node gives a stack-like policy rather than ordering by remaining-cost estimates.

B · incorrect — Appending every new node gives FIFO breadth order rather than heuristic priority.

C · incorrect — Ordering by accumulated path cost g implements uniform-cost selection, not greedy h-only selection.

D · correct — Ordering by the stated evaluation h puts the smallest estimated remaining cost first.

Question 112

In classical propositional logic over a nonempty set of interpretations, which statements are false? In D, “models” means all interpretations. Select all that apply.

  • A. A sentence is said to be invalid iff it is unsatisfiable.
  • B. A sentence is valid if it is satisfiable.
  • C. A sentence which is not invalid is satisfiable.
  • D. A sentence is unsatisfiable if it is false in all models.

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 20

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Translate the statement carefully, then check the scope of its quantifiers, connectives or inference rule. Distinguish guaranteed consequences from plausible generalizations or explanations.

Study-guide sections

AI25 · Propositional logic and models

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI25 · Propositional logic and models

Correct answers (select all): A, B — A sentence is said to be invalid iff it is unsatisfiable.; A sentence is valid if it is satisfiable.

Validity requires truth in every interpretation, while satisfiability requires truth in at least one. A contingent atom can therefore be satisfiable and invalid, refuting both the proposed invalid-unsatisfiable equivalence and the claim that satisfiability implies validity. Not invalid means valid and hence satisfiable in the stated nonempty setting. Unsatisfiable means false in every interpretation, so the remaining two statements are true.

Evidence in the complete study note

A model is an interpretation making a sentence true. Valid means true in every interpretation; satisfiable means true in at least one; unsatisfiable means true in none. Invalid means not valid, and may still be satisfiable. P∨¬P is valid; P is satisfiable but not valid; P∧¬P is unsatisfiable. Entailment KB⊨α means every model of KB also satisfies α.AI25

Choice by choice

A · correct — False: a satisfiable contingent sentence can be invalid without being unsatisfiable.

B · correct — False: truth in one interpretation does not imply truth in every interpretation.

C · incorrect — True: not invalid means valid, which entails satisfiability in the ordinary model setting.

D · incorrect — True: unsatisfiable means there is no interpretation making the sentence true.

  • A. Goal based
  • B. Model based reflex

Study-guide sections

AI07 · Goals, utility and model updates

AI06 · Simple and model-based reflex agents

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI07 · Goals, utility and model updates

AI06 · Simple and model-based reflex agents

Correct answer: A — Goal based

The action selector explicitly consults the desired state and looks ahead over sequences that can reach it. That is the defining goal-based decision criterion. Persistent state also gives the agent a model-based capability, but memory alone does not identify its selection policy. A reflex policy would apply condition-action rules instead of goal-directed lookahead, and utility-based choice would rank degrees of desirability among outcomes.

Evidence in the complete study note

A goal-based agent considers future action sequences that reach a desired state. A utility-based agent compares degrees of desirability and trade-offs, choosing maximum expected utility: EU(a)=Σs P(s|a,evidence)U(s). Reaching the destination is a goal; balancing arrival time, safety and cost requires preferences among outcomes.AI07
Updating an internal state after selecting an action predicts the action’s effect; it does not itself modify the external environment. A stored variable named goal is insufficient to prove a goal-based policy if BEST_ACTION never uses it. Model-based, goal-based, utility-based and learning capabilities can coexist.AI07
A simple reflex agent matches condition–action rules against the current percept only: if dirty, clean. It has no persistent world-state memory. This is adequate when the current observation contains everything needed for its rule, but partial observability can make the same percept require different actions.AI06

Choice by choice

A · correct — Goal-directed lookahead chooses sequences reaching a desired state, matching goal-based action selection.

B · incorrect — The agent maintains a model, but the stated policy uses goal-directed lookahead rather than reflex rules.

C · incorrect — Persistent state and future-sequence evaluation contradict a current-percept-only reflex policy.

D · incorrect — No utility ranking is used; the selector evaluates attainment of the desired state.

AI03 · Agents, percepts and action

AI42 · Distinguish agent categories and components

AI39 · Perception, vision and robotics

Correct answers (select all): B, C — Effectors; Actuators

Actuators and effectors are equivalent general names for the agent’s acting interface here. Sensors instead supply observations. A manipulator can be a particular physical acting device, but it is not the general term covering every agent, including software agents. The scope allows the two synonymous general terms without incorrectly denying that robotic manipulators can carry out actions.

Evidence in the complete study note

An agent perceives an environment through sensors and acts through actuators or effectors. Cameras sense; motors move. Software sensors may be incoming messages and software actions may be API requests. Humans are agents but are not artificial agents.AI03
A generic rule does not distinguish simple from model-based reflex without specifying memory. A goal declaration unused by the action policy does not establish goal-based behavior. “Sensors and effectors” describes interaction, not omniscience or intelligence by itself. Define the mechanical distinction when comparing effectors and actuators as acting components.AI42
Robotics combines mechanical, electrical, control and computing systems to sense, plan and act physically. Components include sensors, controller, power supply, actuators and an end effector. Locomotion may be legged, wheeled or tracked, with trade-offs in terrain, stability and efficiency. Software can act autonomously without being a robot. Humanoid shape is not evidence of general intelligence.AI39

A control agent has incomplete observations, uncertain transition outcomes, actions that affect later decisions, a world that changes during deliberation, and real-valued measurements and controls. Which list matches all these properties?

  • A. Fully observable, discrete, episodic, static.
  • B. Static, episodic, continuous, partially observable.
  • C. Partially observable, non-deterministic, non-episodic, dynamic, continuous.
  • D. Deterministic, sequential (non-episodic), dynamic, continuous.

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Study-guide sections

AI09 · Environment dimensions

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI09 · Environment dimensions

Correct answer: C — Partially observable, non-deterministic, non-episodic, dynamic, continuous.

The scenario establishes each environment dimension directly. Incomplete observations give partial observability; uncertain outcomes give non-determinism; effects on later decisions give sequentiality; ongoing change gives dynamics; and real-valued quantities give continuity. Only one list matches the whole combination. This classification avoids claiming that these dimensions establish a universal numerical ranking of task difficulty.

Evidence in the complete study note

Fully observable means sensors reveal relevant state; partially observable means relevant information is hidden or noisy. Deterministic means state and action determine the next state; stochastic means outcomes involve randomness. Strategic uncertainty about an opponent is distinct from dice-like randomness.AI09
Episodic decisions are independent; sequential decisions affect later situations. Static worlds do not change while deliberating; dynamic ones do. A clock affecting score makes an otherwise static game semidynamic. Discrete quantities have distinct alternatives; continuous quantities vary along real-valued ranges. Known versus unknown concerns knowledge of the transition model, not observability.AI09

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Full observability, episodic independence and a static discrete setting contradict the scenario.

B · incorrect — Partial observability and continuity fit, but static and episodic do not.

C · correct — Partial observability, non-determinism, sequentiality, dynamics and continuity all match.

D · incorrect — The other stated properties fit, but determinism contradicts uncertain transition outcomes.

AI31 · Supervised learning and prediction

AI32 · Unsupervised, semi-supervised and active learning

Correct answers (select all): A, B — Summarization trained on document/reference-summary pairs.; Time-series forecasting trained on history/next-value target pairs.

Supervised training uses paired inputs and target outputs. Document/reference-summary pairs therefore make the summarization task supervised, and history/next-value pairs make the forecasting task supervised. Sequence discovery and clustering without targets instead seek structure in unlabeled data. The labels in the descriptions determine the regime; task names alone would not establish whether summarization or time-series analysis is supervised.

Evidence in the complete study note

Supervised learning fits a mapping from labeled input–target examples. Classification predicts discrete labels, such as institution generations or spam/nonspam; regression predicts numeric quantities, such as prices. Predictive analytics uses historical patterns to forecast outcomes and can use either. Specify the target before choosing a method.AI31
Unsupervised learning seeks structure without target labels: clustering groups similar examples; association finds co-occurrence; dimensionality reduction compresses features. Good clusters have high within-cluster similarity and low between-cluster similarity under an appropriate distance. K-means alternates assignment to nearest centroids and centroid updates.AI32

B · correct — The next value is a numeric target paired with each input history.

C · incorrect — Without target labels, sequence discovery seeks unlabeled structure.

Question 117

A common name used to describe search-based optimization technique based on the principles of Genetics and Natural Selection is ____.

  • A. Genetic algorithms
  • B. Heuristic algorithm
  • C. Hill climbing
  • D. Simulated annealing

Source

  • Mock exam 1 · Question 1

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Check how the method selects its next candidate, what information it uses, and which cost, depth or heuristic assumptions the question supplies.

Study-guide sections

AI20 · Local optimization and evolutionary search

AI-S05 · Related search and game-evaluation methods

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI20 · Local optimization and evolutionary search

AI-S05 · Related search and game-evaluation methods

Correct answer: A — Genetic algorithms.

AI20 names the search method with population, fitness, parent selection, crossover and mutation as a genetic algorithm. That is the specific common name requested by the genetics/natural-selection description. Heuristic algorithm is a broad umbrella rather than this name; hill climbing follows improved neighbors, and simulated annealing is not the population-selection mechanism described.

Evidence in the complete study note

A genetic algorithm maintains a population, evaluates fitness, selects parents, applies crossover and mutation, and repeats replacement. It searches without guaranteeing global optimality. Means–ends analysis selects a difference between current and goal states, chooses an operator reducing it, and recursively solves its preconditions. Neither method is simply A* running backward.AI20
Local search keeps a complete candidate configuration and improves its objective; the path may be irrelevant. Hill climbing chooses better neighbors. First-improvement accepts the first improvement; steepest-ascent examines all neighbors; stochastic variants choose among improvements. Local maxima, plateaus and ridges can stop progress. Random restarts or limited sideways steps can help without guaranteeing success.AI20
Simulated annealing follows a current candidate and randomly samples a neighboring move. It accepts improvements and sometimes accepts worse moves according to a temperature that decreases over time. Unlike genetic search, its defining mechanism is not a population undergoing parent selection, crossover and mutation.AI-S05

Choice by choice

A · correct — This is the specific name of the evolutionary search technique based on fitness, selection and genetic variation.

B · incorrect — Heuristic algorithm is a broad category and does not specifically name the genetics-based population method.

C · incorrect — Hill climbing improves a candidate through neighbors rather than maintaining the described genetic population.

D · incorrect — Simulated annealing is not the named selection/crossover/mutation method defined in the note.

  • B. Over fitting
  • C. Learning curve

AI35 · Generalization and validation

AI-S06 · Prediction, transfer and explicit representations

Correct answer: B — Overfitting.

AI35 directly defines overfitting as fitting training-specific details so performance drops on unseen data. This is the complete failure pattern described in the stem. Underfitting is insufficient fit even on training data; a learning curve is a plot used to inspect performance. Variance may describe sensitivity but does not name the training-versus-generalization failure asked for.

Evidence in the complete study note

Overfitting means fitting training-specific details so performance drops on unseen data; underfitting means the model is too limited or poorly fitted even on training data. A learning curve plots performance against training size or training progress. Complexity control, regularization, pruning and more representative data can help.AI35
Support-vector machines include supervised classification and regression methods. They use support vectors in their decision function rather than being defined by a next-state conditional-dependence assumption. In estimation, variance measures how predictions change across different training samples; overfitting instead names poor generalization caused by fitting training-specific details.AI-S06

Question 121

Which general AI search category uses the problem definition and known costs without a problem-specific estimate of remaining cost to a goal?

  • A. Informed search
  • B. Uninformed search
  • C. Greedy best-first search

AI17 · Heuristics and greedy best-first search

AI-S02 · Ordered lookup versus state-space traversal

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI17 · Heuristics and greedy best-first search

AI-S02 · Ordered lookup versus state-space traversal

Correct answer: B — Uninformed search

Uninformed search uses the problem definition, including legal actions, goal tests and known action costs, without a domain-specific remaining-cost estimate. Informed methods add such guidance, and greedy best-first uses it directly as h. Binary search is a different ordered-lookup algorithm for sorted sequences. The formerly undefined circular-search distractor is replaced with a meaningful search method.

Evidence in the complete study note

A heuristic h(n) estimates remaining cost or evaluates promise using problem-specific knowledge. It can reduce explored work, but computing it also costs time. Uninformed algorithms use only the problem definition and known costs; UCS remains uninformed despite using g.AI17
Binary search exploits the order of a sorted sequence: a comparison narrows the remaining candidate interval instead of exploring arbitrary successor states. Array bisection therefore differs from breadth-first or depth-first traversal of a general state-space graph. A storage container such as an array does not by itself specify FIFO or LIFO frontier behavior.AI-S02
Best-first is a family that orders OPEN by an evaluation function. Greedy best-first uses f=h and removes the smallest estimate, ignoring the cost already paid. It can choose an expensive route, loop without duplicate checks, or follow an infinite misleading branch. On a finite graph with full duplicate handling it is complete, but not generally optimal. Its implicit finite-tree worst case can be O(b^m).AI17

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Informed search adds problem-specific guidance beyond the basic problem definition.

B · correct — Uninformed search uses the problem definition without a heuristic estimate of remaining cost.

C · incorrect — Greedy best-first explicitly uses h, an estimate of remaining cost.

D · incorrect — Binary search narrows a sorted sequence by comparisons; it is a specific ordered-lookup algorithm, not the broad AI search category requested.

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI02 · Four approaches and the Turing test

AI-S07 · Behavior tests, understanding and software tests

Correct answer: C — Turing test

The conversational Turing test evaluates whether a judge can reliably distinguish a machine’s dialogue from a human’s. It supplies an observable behavior criterion rather than proof of understanding. The Chinese-room argument addresses understanding philosophically, response-time experiments test cognitive models empirically, and black-box testing concerns externally visible software functionality. Those are different questions or procedures.

Evidence in the complete study note

The conversational Turing test asks whether a judge can reliably distinguish a machine from a human through their dialogue. It requires language use, knowledge, reasoning and often learning. It tests an operational behavior criterion, not proof of consciousness. Cognitive models can be tested against response times, errors and psychological experiments.AI02
Searle’s Chinese-room argument challenges whether executing formal symbol-manipulation rules is sufficient for understanding. It is a philosophical argument about understanding, not the conversational judge-and-hidden-participant procedure of the Turing test.AI-S07
Black-box software testing examines externally visible functionality without inspecting implementation internals. A specification may concern any software behavior; this testing method does not by itself require conversational indistinguishability from a human.AI-S07

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — The Chinese-room argument concerns whether formal symbol manipulation suffices for understanding; it is not the judge-and-conversation test.

B · incorrect — A response-time experiment evaluates a cognitive model against human measurements rather than applying conversational indistinguishability.

C · correct — The conversational Turing test uses this judge-and-hidden-participant criterion.

D · incorrect — Black-box testing checks external software functionality without inspecting internals; it does not inherently require humanlike conversation.

An RL agent observes state information, takes an action, receives reward and a new observation, and improves its policy to maximize expected cumulative reward. Tokenization divides text into processing units; tokens may be words, punctuation or subwords. POS tagging assigns grammatical roles; named-entity recognition identifies people, organizations and locations. Parsing identifies grammatical structure; semantics concerns meaning; discourse links sentences; pragmatics uses context and speaker intent. Sentiment analysis predicts evaluative tone. Unsupervised learning seeks structure without target labels: clustering groups similar examples; association finds co-occurrence; dimensionality reduction compresses features. AI09 · Environment dimensions

Correct answer: D — Partially observable

The sensors cannot determine complete state; this is precisely partial observability. It says nothing about transition randomness. Evidence: PDF 13.

Evidence in the complete study note

Fully observable means sensors reveal relevant state; partially observable means relevant information is hidden or noisy. Deterministic means state and action determine the next state; stochastic means outcomes involve randomness. Strategic uncertainty about an opponent is distinct from dice-like randomness.AI09
Episodic decisions are independent; sequential decisions affect later situations. Static worlds do not change while deliberating; dynamic ones do. A clock affecting score makes an otherwise static game semidynamic. Discrete quantities have distinct alternatives; continuous quantities vary along real-valued ranges. Known versus unknown concerns knowledge of the transition model, not observability.AI09

Propositional atoms represent whole true-or-false claims. ¬P negates; P∧Q requires both; P∨Q requires at least one; P→Q is false only when P is true and Q false; P↔Q requires matching truth values. Thus P→Q ≡ ¬P∨Q. De Morgan gives ¬(P∧Q) ≡ ¬P∨¬Q.AI25

AI03 · Agents, percepts and action

AI04 · Rationality and performance

Correct answer: B — Percept sequence

A percept is one observation, while a percept sequence is the entire observation history. A performance measure defines success instead of storing observations. Knowledge may include prior facts and inferences beyond the observation history, and an action is selected behavior rather than observed input. Replacing the overly broad perception option supplies the precise established term without changing the agent-history concept.

Evidence in the complete study note

A percept is one observation; a percept sequence is the entire observation history. An agent function maps percept sequences to actions: f:P*→A. An agent program implements that mapping on an architecture; agent = architecture + program. Environment means the setting in which it senses and acts, not merely the search space. Autonomy means relying substantially on experience rather than only a designer’s prior instructions.AI03
A performance measure defines success externally: safety, useful deliveries, elapsed time, or cost. Rationality depends on that measure, prior knowledge, percept history, and available actions. A rational agent selects the action with the best expected performance given its information.AI04

Question 131

The simple strategy in which the root node is expanded first, then all successors are expanded next, layer by layer, refers to:

  • A. Greedy best-first search
  • B. Depth-first search (DFS)
  • C. Depth limited search (DLS)
  • D. Breadth-first search (BFS)

Sources

  • Computer Science Exit Exam · Sene 2016 · Question 7-3

  • Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 206

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Check how the method selects its next candidate, what information it uses, and which cost, depth or heuristic assumptions the question supplies.

Study-guide sections

AI13 · Breadth-first search

AI14 · Depth-first search

AI16 · Depth limits, iterative deepening and two directions

AI17 · Heuristics and greedy best-first search

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI13 · Breadth-first search

AI14 · Depth-first search

AI16 · Depth limits, iterative deepening and two directions

AI17 · Heuristics and greedy best-first search

Correct answer: D — Breadth-first search (BFS)

Expanding every node at one level before the next is the stated BFS order. Evidence: PDF 19.

Evidence in the complete study note

BFS removes the oldest frontier entry using a FIFO queue. Start with the root, remove the head, test it, append unseen successors at the tail, and repeat. It explores depths 0,1,2,… and is complete for finite b and a finite-depth goal. It minimizes number of edges, so minimum cost requires equal positive step costs.AI13
DFS follows the deepest pending branch using a LIFO stack or recursion. FILO means the same order as LIFO. With the same children as BFS, a left-first DFS visits S,A,C before B; push rightmost children first to pop the leftmost first.AI14
DLS runs DFS to depth ℓ and reports cutoff separately from failure. It misses goals deeper than ℓ. Iterative deepening runs DLS with limits 0,1,2,…; for finite b it finds the shallowest solution with O(b^d) time and O(bd) frontier space, optimal for equal step costs. Repeated shallow work is small compared with the deepest level.AI16
Best-first is a family that orders OPEN by an evaluation function. Greedy best-first uses f=h and removes the smallest estimate, ignoring the cost already paid. It can choose an expensive route, loop without duplicate checks, or follow an infinite misleading branch. On a finite graph with full duplicate handling it is complete, but not generally optimal. Its implicit finite-tree worst case can be O(b^m).AI17

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Ranks by estimated goal distance. See PDF p. 19.

B · incorrect — Follows a path deeply before siblings. See PDF p. 19.

C · incorrect — Restricts DFS to a bound. See PDF p. 19.

D · correct — Exact layer-order expansion. See PDF p. 19.

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI24 · Represent knowledge for inference

AI17 · Heuristics and greedy best-first search

Correct answer: C — Theory of blind searching

Reasoning uses knowledge and a specified methodology to derive conclusions from premises. Logical argument and inference are therefore appropriate descriptions. Blind search is instead a search strategy that explores alternatives without heuristic guidance; it does not define reasoning as a whole. Clarifying the incomplete knowledge-system option into a claim about deriving conclusions leaves the intended search-versus-inference distinction as the unique exception.

Evidence in the complete study note

Knowledge representation encodes facts, objects, relations, events and rules so a machine can use them. Syntax defines legal expressions; semantics defines their meaning. A knowledge base stores assertions; an inference system derives consequences. Declarative knowledge says what is true; procedural knowledge specifies how to act.AI24
A heuristic h(n) estimates remaining cost or evaluates promise using problem-specific knowledge. It can reduce explored work, but computing it also costs time. Uninformed algorithms use only the problem definition and known costs; UCS remains uninformed despite using g.AI17

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Using knowledge to derive conclusions is a valid characterization, so it is not the exception.

B · incorrect — Logical argument and drawing inferences describe reasoning, so this is not a false characterization for the negative question.

C · correct — Blind search is one search strategy rather than a definition of reasoning.

D · incorrect — Deriving a conclusion from premises using a methodology describes reasoning and does not satisfy the negative question.

Question 133

Which reasoning technique applies valid inference rules so that true premises guarantee a true conclusion?

  • A. Abductive reasoning
  • B. Analogical reasoning
  • C. Deductive reasoning
  • D. Inductive reasoning

Adapted from

  • Computer Science Exit Exam · Sene 2016 · Question 20-1

  • Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 204

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Translate the statement carefully, then check the scope of its quantifiers, connectives or inference rule. Distinguish guaranteed consequences from plausible generalizations or explanations.

Study-guide sections

AI28 · Deduction, induction and abduction

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI28 · Deduction, induction and abduction

Correct answer: C — Deductive reasoning

Deductive reasoning uses truth-preserving inference: when the premises are true and the rule is valid, the conclusion must be true. Rules in a broad sense are not sufficient to identify deduction, since many reasoning methods use procedures. Induction generalizes from cases, abduction proposes explanations, and analogy transfers conclusions across similarities; these do not supply the stated logical guarantee.

Evidence in the complete study note

Deduction applies truth-preserving rules: all people are mortal; Ada is a person; therefore Ada is mortal. Induction generalizes observations to a broader rule and can be overturned by new examples. Abduction proposes a plausible explanation: wet ground suggests rain, although sprinklers could explain it. Analogy transfers a pattern between similar situations.AI28
Classical logical entailment is monotonic: adding premises preserves previous consequences. Default reasoning can be nonmonotonic: infer a bird usually flies, then withdraw this when told it is a penguin. Common-sense defaults are useful with incomplete knowledge, but are not guaranteed truths. Blind search is a search strategy, not a definition of reasoning.AI28

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Abduction proposes plausible explanatory hypotheses that can still be false.

B · incorrect — Analogy transfers a conclusion from a similar case without a truth-preservation guarantee.

C · correct — Valid deductive inference preserves truth from premises to conclusion.

D · incorrect — Induction generalizes beyond the observed cases and remains revisable.

Question 134

For A* tree search with an admissible heuristic and positive step costs, what is the intended benefit of using the heuristic alongside accumulated edge costs?

  • A. To seek a least-cost path while potentially reducing expansions through heuristic guidance.
  • B. To find the path with the maximum distance from the start to the goal node
  • C. To find paths with non-optimal searches from node to the goal node
  • D. To find the path with the maximum cost from the start to the goal node

Adapted from

  • Computer Science Exit Exam · Sene 2016 · Question 22-3

  • Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 209

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Check how the method selects its next candidate, what information it uses, and which cost, depth or heuristic assumptions the question supplies.

Study-guide sections

AI18 · Admissibility, consistency and A*

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI18 · Admissibility, consistency and A*

Correct answer: A — To seek a least-cost path while potentially reducing expansions through heuristic guidance.

A* adds accumulated cost g to an admissible remaining-cost estimate h. Under the stated tree-search conditions, this supports least-cost solutions, while useful heuristic guidance can reduce expansions. It does not guarantee a speed improvement for every problem or heuristic. Maximizing distance or cost is a different objective, and deliberately seeking nonoptimal paths is not the benefit described.

Evidence in the complete study note

A* orders by f(n)=g(n)+h(n). Admissibility means 0≤h(n)≤h*(n), the true cheapest remaining cost. Consistency means h(n)≤c(n,n′)+h(n′) on every edge, with h(goal)=0; it implies admissibility on states with goal paths. Consistency makes f nondecreasing along a path.AI18
Admissibility suffices for optimal A* tree search; graph search that never reopens CLOSED states normally requires consistency. With an admissible inconsistent heuristic, reopen states when g improves. Test a goal when removed at minimum f. Completeness also needs finite branching and positive lower-bounded costs in infinite spaces. Worst-case time and memory can be exponential; no heuristic universally guarantees speed.AI18

Choice by choice

A · correct — An admissible remaining-cost estimate supports optimal tree search and can guide exploration toward useful candidates.

B · incorrect — A* minimizes total path cost; it does not seek maximum path length.

C · incorrect — Nonoptimality is not the purpose of admissible A* tree search.

D · incorrect — A* seeks minimum, not maximum, total cost.

Correct answer: D — A* Search

A* uses a best-first priority frontier ordered by g+h. Consistency provides the standard guarantee for graph search that permanently closes states, with the stated cost and goal-test conditions. IDA* also uses f values but organizes repeated depth-first threshold searches instead. Greedy search omits g, and UCS omits h. The frontier organization distinguishes the algorithms rather than a worst-case complexity shared by several methods.

Evidence in the complete study note

A* orders by f(n)=g(n)+h(n). Admissibility means 0≤h(n)≤h*(n), the true cheapest remaining cost. Consistency means h(n)≤c(n,n′)+h(n′) on every edge, with h(goal)=0; it implies admissibility on states with goal paths. Consistency makes f nondecreasing along a path.AI18
Admissibility suffices for optimal A* tree search; graph search that never reopens CLOSED states normally requires consistency. With an admissible inconsistent heuristic, reopen states when g improves. Test a goal when removed at minimum f. Completeness also needs finite branching and positive lower-bounded costs in infinite spaces. Worst-case time and memory can be exponential; no heuristic universally guarantees speed.AI18
Bidirectional search grows from start and goal until frontiers connect. With suitable reverse actions, meeting tests and equal-cost BFS, time and space may fall to O(b^(d/2)). Weighted variants require a sound stopping bound; the first intersection need not be cheapest. IDA* deepens an f=g+h threshold rather than only a depth limit.AI16
Best-first is a family that orders OPEN by an evaluation function. Greedy best-first uses f=h and removes the smallest estimate, ignoring the cost already paid. It can choose an expensive route, loop without duplicate checks, or follow an infinite misleading branch. On a finite graph with full duplicate handling it is complete, but not generally optimal. Its implicit finite-tree worst case can be O(b^m).AI17
UCS uses a priority queue ordered by actual accumulated path cost g(n).AI15

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — IDA* repeats depth-first searches under increasing f thresholds rather than retaining this single priority frontier.

B · incorrect — Greedy best-first uses h alone and does not have the stated cost-aware priority.

C · incorrect — UCS uses g alone, without the heuristic term.

D · correct — A* uses g+h; consistency supports optimality when graph states are closed without reopening.

Which general term denotes an entity that perceives its environment through sensors and acts on it through effectors?

AI40 · Expert systems and choosing methods

Correct answer: D — Agent

An agent is defined by perceiving an environment and acting on it through sensors and effectors. The acting mechanism may be physical or software-based. An API can expose operations used by an agent, and an expert system can contribute domain reasoning, but neither names the general entity defined here. Intelligence is a capability rather than the entity itself.

Evidence in the complete study note

An agent perceives an environment through sensors and acts through actuators or effectors. Cameras sense; motors move. Software sensors may be incoming messages and software actions may be API requests. Humans are agents but are not artificial agents.AI03
An expert system applies specialized knowledge to a domain such as equipment diagnosis. The domain expert supplies expertise; the knowledge engineer elicits and encodes it; the inference engine reasons over a knowledge base and working facts. The user interface handles interaction; an explanation facility presents why or how a conclusion was reached.AI40
An application programming interface (API) exposes defined operations through which software requests functionality. It can be an interface used by an agent, but the interface alone is not the general entity that perceives an environment and selects actions.AI-S06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — An API exposes software operations; it may support an agent’s actions but is not the general perceiving-and-acting entity.

B · incorrect — An expert system is a specialized knowledge-based application, not the general term for every sensing-and-acting entity.

C · incorrect — Intelligence is a capability, not the name of the defined entity.

D · correct — Agent is the general term for an entity with this perception-and-action interaction.

Question 138

A new dataset has no target labels. The objective is to discover its groups or structure, with neither interaction rewards nor reuse of a pretrained model. Which learning regime applies?

  • A. Reinforcement learning
  • B. Unsupervised learning
  • C. Transfer learning
  • D. Supervised learning

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam collection · Question 78

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify the training feedback, prediction target or measured error. Keep learning objectives separate from model architecture and data modality.

Study-guide sections

AI32 · Unsupervised, semi-supervised and active learning

AI31 · Supervised learning and prediction

AI33 · Reinforcement learning

AI-S06 · Prediction, transfer and explicit representations

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI32 · Unsupervised, semi-supervised and active learning

AI31 · Supervised learning and prediction

AI33 · Reinforcement learning

AI-S06 · Prediction, transfer and explicit representations

Correct answer: B — Unsupervised learning

The objective is structure discovery without target labels, which defines unsupervised learning. The stem separately excludes action-reward interaction and reuse of a pretrained model. Those exclusions distinguish reinforcement feedback and transfer learning from this task. Transfer learning describes a reuse strategy rather than a label-availability regime and can be combined with different learning objectives.

Evidence in the complete study note

Unsupervised learning seeks structure without target labels: clustering groups similar examples; association finds co-occurrence; dimensionality reduction compresses features. Good clusters have high within-cluster similarity and low between-cluster similarity under an appropriate distance. K-means alternates assignment to nearest centroids and centroid updates.AI32
Supervised learning fits a mapping from labeled input–target examples. Classification predicts discrete labels, such as institution generations or spam/nonspam; regression predicts numeric quantities, such as prices. Predictive analytics uses historical patterns to forecast outcomes and can use either. Specify the target before choosing a method.AI31
An RL agent observes state information, takes an action, receives reward and a new observation, and improves its policy to maximize expected cumulative reward. Rewards evaluate outcomes rather than supply the correct action label. Rewards may be delayed; not every correct-looking action receives immediate reward.AI33
Transfer learning reuses representations or a model learned on an earlier task for a new task, for example adapting pretrained image features to new image classes. This is a reuse strategy, not a specification that the new task has no labels or rewards.AI-S06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Reinforcement learning requires a reward-based interaction objective, which is excluded.

B · correct — Unsupervised learning discovers structure in data without supplied target labels.

C · incorrect — Transfer learning concerns reuse of prior learned representations or models; no such reuse is present.

D · incorrect — Supervised learning requires target outputs paired with the inputs.

Question 140

A techniques for generating plans with conditionals and loops are almost identical to those for generating programs from logical specifications is called__

  • A. Automatic learning
  • B. Automatic goal testing
  • C. Automatic monitoring
  • D. Automatic programming

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam collection · Question 94

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Read the relevant agent component, action-selection criterion or environment dimension. Use only properties established by the description.

Study-guide sections

AI11 · Formulate before searching

AI08 · Learning-agent components

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI11 · Formulate before searching

AI08 · Learning-agent components

Correct answer: D — Automatic programming

Automatic programming, also called program synthesis, constructs a program that satisfies a specification. Generating conditional plans or loops is analogous because the output must implement the required behavior. Learning changes performance through experience, goal testing checks whether a candidate succeeds, and monitoring checks execution. None of those by itself names the specification-to-program construction task.

Evidence in the complete study note

In route finding, states are cities, actions are roads, successors are neighboring cities, and path cost is accumulated distance or time. A solution is a legal path ending at a goal; an optimal solution has minimum cost. Automatic programming or program synthesis searches for a program satisfying a specification; conditional plans and loops require richer representations than a fixed action list.AI11
Learning is improvement on task T, measured by P, through experience E. For spam filtering, T is classifying email, E is past labeled messages, and P might be recall at a required precision. Exploration trades immediate reward for information; exploitation uses the best action currently known. Learning can improve reflex, goal-based or utility-based agents.AI08
First formulate the goal; then formulate the problem by specifying initial state, legal actions, transition model, goal test, and action costs. Search selects a sequence; execution applies it. A state abstracts away irrelevant world details.AI11

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Learning improves performance through experience rather than specifically synthesizing a program from logical requirements.

B · incorrect — A goal test checks whether a candidate meets the goal; it does not generate a program from its specification.

C · incorrect — Monitoring checks an executing system rather than generating a program from a specification.

D · correct — Automatic programming or program synthesis constructs a program meeting a specification, including conditional or looping behavior.

Question 143

Which representation system matches IF-THEN production rules against working memory and applies a selected rule to derive a conclusion or action?

  • A. Semantic networks
  • B. Neural networks
  • C. Production systems
  • D. Bayesian networks

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 626

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify the training feedback, prediction target or measured error. Keep learning objectives separate from model architecture and data modality.

Study-guide sections

AI24 · Represent knowledge for inference

AI29 · Probability and uncertain models

AI34 · Neural networks and deep learning

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI24 · Represent knowledge for inference

AI29 · Probability and uncertain models

AI34 · Neural networks and deep learning

Correct answer: C — Production systems

A production system uses IF-THEN rules whose conditions are matched against working memory; an applicable rule is selected and applied. Semantic networks encode concept relationships, neural networks learn weighted representations, and Bayesian networks encode probabilistic dependencies. All can support reasoning in broader systems, so the distinctive feature here is the explicit production-rule cycle rather than inference in general.

Evidence in the complete study note

A semantic network connects concept nodes by labeled relations such as is-a. Frames describe stereotyped entities through slots, values and defaults. Production systems use IF conditions THEN conclusions or actions, matching rules against working memory and selecting among applicable rules. A graph suits relationships such as frequently bought together; frames suit attributes. No representation is always best for recommendation without task requirements.AI24
A Bayesian network is a directed acyclic graph with conditional probability tables; its joint distribution factors as the product of each node’s probability given its parents. A Markov model assumes the next state depends on the current state rather than the entire past. These represent uncertainty; fuzzy membership represents a different issue.AI29
Feedforward networks pass signals toward outputs without recurrent state loops; recurrent networks carry state across sequence steps. Training adjusts weights, often through gradients and backpropagation. Backpropagation is not the same as a recurrent connection. Deep learning uses multiple representation layers and can learn features from images, sound and text. CNNs share filters across image locations. ANN is a brain-inspired abstraction, not a literal brain simulation; DL⊂ML⊂AI.AI34

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Semantic networks represent concepts and labeled relationships, not this working-memory production-rule cycle.

B · incorrect — Neural networks compute through weighted units and learned representations rather than the specified rule-matching architecture.

C · correct — Production systems match condition–action or condition–conclusion rules against working memory.

D · incorrect — Bayesian networks represent conditional probabilistic dependencies rather than the stated production-rule mechanism.

  • B. Inductive reasoning
  • C. Abductive reasoning
  • D. Probabilistic reasoning

AI28 · Deduction, induction and abduction

AI29 · Probability and uncertain models

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI28 · Deduction, induction and abduction

AI29 · Probability and uncertain models

Correct answer: B — Inductive reasoning

Specific facts generalized into a conclusion define induction. The conclusion is supported rather than logically guaranteed by the finite examples. Evidence: PDF 53.

Evidence in the complete study note

Deduction applies truth-preserving rules: all people are mortal; Ada is a person; therefore Ada is mortal. Induction generalizes observations to a broader rule and can be overturned by new examples. Abduction proposes a plausible explanation: wet ground suggests rain, although sprinklers could explain it. Analogy transfers a pattern between similar situations.AI28
Probability describes uncertainty about events. P(¬A)=1−P(A); P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B), for P(B)>0. Bayes gives P(H|E)=P(E|H)P(H)/P(E): posterior equals likelihood times prior divided by evidence probability. For mutually exclusive exhaustive hypotheses, P(E)=ΣiP(E|Hi)P(Hi).AI29

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Typically general premises to specific conclusion. See PDF p. 53.

B · correct — Exact specific-to-general pattern. See PDF p. 53.

C · incorrect — Seeks most likely explanation for observations. See PDF p. 53.

D · incorrect — Uses probability to express uncertainty, not this defining direction. See PDF p. 53.
