Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI34 · Neural networks and deep learning

AI33 · Reinforcement learning

Correct answer: D — DL⊂ML⊂AI.

AI34 explicitly gives deep learning inside machine learning inside AI. Deep neural architectures are a subset of learning methods, and learning is one component of the broader intelligence field, which also includes planning and reasoning. Every other ordering reverses at least one of these stated inclusions.

Evidence in the complete study note

Feedforward networks pass signals toward outputs without recurrent state loops; recurrent networks carry state across sequence steps. Training adjusts weights, often through gradients and backpropagation. Backpropagation is not the same as a recurrent connection. Deep learning uses multiple representation layers and can learn features from images, sound and text. CNNs share filters across image locations. ANN is a brain-inspired abstraction, not a literal brain simulation; DL⊂ML⊂AI.AI34
An RL agent observes state information, takes an action, receives reward and a new observation, and improves its policy to maximize expected cumulative reward. Rewards evaluate outcomes rather than supply the correct action label. Rewards may be delayed; not every correct-looking action receives immediate reward.AI33

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — This wrongly puts AI inside machine learning rather than the reverse.

B · incorrect — Both inclusions are reversed relative to the note’s hierarchy.

C · incorrect — Machine learning contains deep learning, not the reverse.

D · correct — Deep learning is contained in machine learning, which is contained in AI.

Question 224

A recommendation system must directly represent products and labeled “frequently bought together” relationships, then traverse those relationships to find connected products. Which listed representation most directly fits that requirement?

  • A. Rule-based IF-THEN logic
  • B. Frames describing product attributes
  • C. Graph-based model with products as nodes and relationships as edges
  • D. Probabilistic Bayesian network of user demographics

Adapted from

  • Artificial Intelligence review questions · Question 50

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Read the definition and the classification axis requested; distinguish the defining purpose from supporting techniques or implementation resources.

Study-guide sections

AI24 · Represent knowledge for inference

AI29 · Probability and uncertain models

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

AI24 · Represent knowledge for inference

AI29 · Probability and uncertain models

Correct answer: C — Graph-based model with products as nodes and relationships as edges

A semantic graph represents entities as nodes and their labeled relationships as edges, making connected products directly traversable. Frames primarily organize attributes, rules express conditions and conclusions, and a Bayesian demographic model represents uncertain dependencies rather than the requested product-edge structure. The answer follows the explicit relational representation requirement; it does not claim that graphs are universally best for every recommendation system.

Evidence in the complete study note

A semantic network connects concept nodes by labeled relations such as is-a. Frames describe stereotyped entities through slots, values and defaults. Production systems use IF conditions THEN conclusions or actions, matching rules against working memory and selecting among applicable rules. A graph suits relationships such as frequently bought together; frames suit attributes. No representation is always best for recommendation without task requirements.AI24
A Bayesian network is a directed acyclic graph with conditional probability tables; its joint distribution factors as the product of each node’s probability given its parents. A Markov model assumes the next state depends on the current state rather than the entire past. These represent uncertainty; fuzzy membership represents a different issue.AI29

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Rules can encode recommendations, but do not directly provide the requested product-node relationship structure.

B · incorrect — Frames describe product attributes rather than making product-to-product links the primary structure.

C · correct — Products as nodes and labeled relationships as edges directly support the required traversal.

D · incorrect — A demographic Bayesian network models uncertain dependencies rather than the specified product-edge structure.

Question 225

What is the difference between supervised and unsupervised learning?

    Source

    • Artificial Intelligence review questions · Question 1

    Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

    Identify the training feedback, prediction target or measured error. Keep learning objectives separate from model architecture and data modality.

    Study-guide sections

    AI31 · Supervised learning and prediction

    AI32 · Unsupervised, semi-supervised and active learning

    Answer & Detailed Explanation

    Study-guide references

    AI31 · Supervised learning and prediction

    AI32 · Unsupervised, semi-supervised and active learning

    Answer: Supervised learning fits labeled input–target examples; unsupervised learning discovers structure without target labels.

    AI31 defines supervised learning through labels, with classification for discrete targets and regression for numeric targets. AI32 defines unsupervised discovery, including clustering, association and dimensionality reduction. The distinction is the supplied training feedback, not whether the data are images, text or numbers; the same modality can support either regime.

    Evidence in the complete study note

    Supervised learning fits a mapping from labeled input–target examples. Classification predicts discrete labels, such as institution generations or spam/nonspam; regression predicts numeric quantities, such as prices. Predictive analytics uses historical patterns to forecast outcomes and can use either. Specify the target before choosing a method.AI31
    Unsupervised learning seeks structure without target labels: clustering groups similar examples; association finds co-occurrence; dimensionality reduction compresses features. Good clusters have high within-cluster similarity and low between-cluster similarity under an appropriate distance. K-means alternates assignment to nearest centroids and centroid updates.AI32

    Question 226

    Under what search and heuristic conditions does A* find a least-cost path, and why?

      Adapted from

      • Artificial Intelligence review questions · Question 2

      Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

      Check how the method selects its next candidate, what information it uses, and which cost, depth or heuristic assumptions the question supplies.

      Study-guide sections

      AI18 · Admissibility, consistency and A*

      Answer & Detailed Explanation

      Study-guide references

      AI18 · Admissibility, consistency and A*

      Answer: A* is optimal under its heuristic and search assumptions: admissible tree search, or consistent graph search without reopening; otherwise reopen improved states.

      With admissible h, A* tree search uses f=g+h as a lower bound on solution cost through each frontier node. Removing a minimum-f goal cannot skip a cheaper represented solution. Graph search that never reopens closed states normally requires consistency; with an admissible inconsistent heuristic, improved states must be reopened. Goal testing is on removal. Finite branching and positive lower-bounded step costs supply the usual infinite-space completeness conditions.

      Evidence in the complete study note

      A* orders by f(n)=g(n)+h(n). Admissibility means 0≤h(n)≤h*(n), the true cheapest remaining cost. Consistency means h(n)≤c(n,n′)+h(n′) on every edge, with h(goal)=0; it implies admissibility on states with goal paths. Consistency makes f nondecreasing along a path.AI18
      Admissibility suffices for optimal A* tree search; graph search that never reopens CLOSED states normally requires consistency. With an admissible inconsistent heuristic, reopen states when g improves. Test a goal when removed at minimum f. Completeness also needs finite branching and positive lower-bounded costs in infinite spaces. Worst-case time and memory can be exponential; no heuristic universally guarantees speed.AI18

      Question 227

      What is the Turing Test and what does it measure?

        Source

        • Artificial Intelligence review questions · Question 3

        Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

        Read the definition and the classification axis requested; distinguish the defining purpose from supporting techniques or implementation resources.

        Study-guide sections

        AI02 · Four approaches and the Turing test

        Answer & Detailed Explanation

        Study-guide references

        AI02 · Four approaches and the Turing test

        Answer: The conversational Turing test asks a judge to distinguish machine from human through dialogue; it measures humanlike behavior, not consciousness.

        AI02 sets the observable criterion: whether a judge can reliably tell a machine’s conversation from a human’s. Language use, knowledge, reasoning and often learning support the performance. Passing would meet this operational behavioral standard, but it does not prove consciousness, actual understanding or that the machine internally thinks in the same way as a human.

        Evidence in the complete study note

        The conversational Turing test asks whether a judge can reliably distinguish a machine from a human through their dialogue. It requires language use, knowledge, reasoning and often learning. It tests an operational behavior criterion, not proof of consciousness. Cognitive models can be tested against response times, errors and psychological experiments.AI02

        Question 228

        What is the difference between precision and recall?

          Source

          • Artificial Intelligence review questions · Question 4

          Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

          Identify the training feedback, prediction target or measured error. Keep learning objectives separate from model architecture and data modality.

          Study-guide sections

          AI36 · Measure the right errors

          Answer & Detailed Explanation

          Study-guide references

          AI36 · Measure the right errors

          Answer: Precision=TP/(TP+FP): how many predicted positives are correct. Recall=TP/(TP+FN): how many actual positives are found.

          AI36 distinguishes precision’s predicted-positive denominator from recall’s actual-positive denominator. False positives reduce precision; false negatives reduce recall. With TP=30, FP=10 and FN=20, precision is 30/40=75% and recall is 30/50=60%. The positive class and zero-denominator convention should be fixed before comparing scores.

          Evidence in the complete study note

          With a fixed positive class, TP means true positives, FP false positive predictions, FN missed positives, TN true negatives. Accuracy=(TP+TN)/N; precision=TP/(TP+FP); recall=TP/(TP+FN); F1=2PR/(P+R). State the averaging and zero-denominator convention when relevant.AI36

          Question 229

          Why is tokenization important in natural language processing?

            Source

            • Artificial Intelligence review questions · Question 5

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Match the input, output and purpose to the appropriate language, perception or physical-action task.

            Study-guide sections

            AI37 · Language processing tasks

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            AI37 · Language processing tasks

            Answer: Tokenization divides text into processing units such as words, punctuation or subwords so later NLP stages can operate on a consistent input sequence.

            AI37 defines tokenization as dividing text into processing units and lists several permitted granularities. Establishing that sequence lets later tagging, recognition and parsing refer to units consistently. Tokens need not equal whitespace-separated words, and tokenization by itself does not determine grammatical structure or resolve word meaning; those belong to later analyses.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            NLP interprets and generates human language: translation, dialogue, summarization, question answering and text generation. Speech recognition converts audio to text; speech synthesis generates speech. They overlap language processing but solve different input/output tasks.AI37
            Tokenization divides text into processing units; tokens may be words, punctuation or subwords. POS tagging assigns grammatical roles; named-entity recognition identifies people, organizations and locations. Parsing identifies grammatical structure; semantics concerns meaning; discourse links sentences; pragmatics uses context and speaker intent. Sentiment analysis predicts evaluative tone. Ambiguity can occur at every level: “bank” has multiple senses, and “I saw the man with a telescope” has multiple attachments.AI37

            Question 230

            Which AI approach most directly supports understanding biological intelligence behavior as a scientific goal?

            • A. Weak AI
            • B. Applied AI
            • C. Cognitive AI
            • D. Strong AI

            Source

            • Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 2

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Read the definition and the classification axis requested; distinguish the defining purpose from supporting techniques or implementation resources.

            Study-guide sections

            AI01 · AI capabilities and scope

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            AI01 · AI capabilities and scope

            Correct answer: C — Cognitive AI.

            AI01 explicitly describes cognitive AI as using computational models to investigate biological intelligence, making it the direct scientific-goal match. Applied AI emphasizes useful solutions. Narrow AI describes capability scope, while strong AI has a philosophical understanding sense; neither is the named research approach for testing models against biological behavior.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Artificial intelligence studies systems that perform tasks requiring intelligence: reasoning, learning, planning, perception and language. Applied AI builds useful solutions; cognitive AI uses computational models to investigate biological intelligence. A model should be compared with human behavior or experimental observations before claiming it explains human thought.AI01
            Narrow or weak AI addresses bounded tasks, such as face recognition, spam filtering or a voice assistant. General AI denotes broad competence transferable across domains; strong AI also has a philosophical meaning involving actual understanding. Do not equate a humanoid body, autonomous vehicle, or many features with general intelligence.AI01

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Weak AI denotes bounded capability rather than the specific scientific modeling goal.

            B · incorrect — Applied AI builds useful solutions rather than primarily explaining biological intelligence.

            C · correct — Cognitive AI uses computational models to investigate biological intelligence and behavior.

            D · incorrect — Strong AI concerns broad or actual-understanding claims, not this specific empirical modeling approach.

            Question 231

            Why is Greedy Best-First Search not guaranteed to be optimal or complete?

            • A. It ignores path cost g( n) and relies only on h( n)
            • B. It always chooses the shallowest node
            • C. It expands nodes in FIFO order
            • D. It requires full knowledge of the goal state in advance

            Source

            • Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 8

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Check how the method selects its next candidate, what information it uses, and which cost, depth or heuristic assumptions the question supplies.

            Study-guide sections

            AI17 · Heuristics and greedy best-first search

            AI19 · Work a heuristic-search example

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            AI17 · Heuristics and greedy best-first search

            AI19 · Work a heuristic-search example

            Correct answer: A — It uses h alone, ignoring accumulated g.

            AI17 says greedy best-first chooses f=h and can take an expensive route or follow an infinite misleading branch. Ignoring g explains nonoptimality, while cycles or infinite paths without appropriate handling explain failure of completeness. On a finite graph with full duplicate handling it is complete, so the lack of a general guarantee does not mean every implementation fails.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Best-first is a family that orders OPEN by an evaluation function. Greedy best-first uses f=h and removes the smallest estimate, ignoring the cost already paid. It can choose an expensive route, loop without duplicate checks, or follow an infinite misleading branch. On a finite graph with full duplicate handling it is complete, but not generally optimal. Its implicit finite-tree worst case can be O(b^m).AI17
            For S→A cost 2, S→B cost 1, A→G cost 2, B→G cost 10, set h(A)=2, h(B)=1, h(G)=0. After expanding S, greedy chooses B because 1<2 and can then choose G, returning cost 11. A* compares A:f=2+2=4 and B:f=1+1=2; after B, its G entry costs 11. It next expands A and replaces G with cost 4, which is removed and accepted.AI19

            Choice by choice

            A · correct — Using only h ignores total path cost and can follow misleading or unbounded branches.

            B · incorrect — Shallowest-first describes breadth-first order rather than greedy heuristic order.

            C · incorrect — FIFO is breadth-first queue behavior, not minimum-h priority selection.

            D · incorrect — Heuristics estimate promise; exact full goal-state knowledge is not required by the algorithm.

            Question 232

            Which search strategy tries to expand the node that is closest to the goal, on the grounds that this is likely to lead to a solution quickly; Thus, it evaluates nodes by using just the heuristic function: f ( n) = h ( n).

            • A. Uniform-cost search
            • B. Greedy best-first search
            • C. Depth-first search
            • D. A* search

            Source

            • Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 23

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Check how the method selects its next candidate, what information it uses, and which cost, depth or heuristic assumptions the question supplies.

            Study-guide sections

            AI17 · Heuristics and greedy best-first search

            AI15 · Uniform-cost search and Dijkstra

            AI18 · Admissibility, consistency and A*

            AI14 · Depth-first search

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            AI17 · Heuristics and greedy best-first search

            AI15 · Uniform-cost search and Dijkstra

            AI18 · Admissibility, consistency and A*

            AI14 · Depth-first search

            Correct answer: B — Greedy best-first search.

            AI17 explicitly defines greedy best-first by removing the smallest remaining-cost estimate h while ignoring paid cost g. This is exactly the stem’s equation. UCS uses g, A* combines g and h, and DFS uses depth/stack discipline rather than a minimum heuristic evaluation.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Best-first is a family that orders OPEN by an evaluation function. Greedy best-first uses f=h and removes the smallest estimate, ignoring the cost already paid. It can choose an expensive route, loop without duplicate checks, or follow an infinite misleading branch. On a finite graph with full duplicate handling it is complete, but not generally optimal. Its implicit finite-tree worst case can be O(b^m).AI17
            UCS uses a priority queue ordered by actual accumulated path cost g(n). Remove a minimum-g node; accept a goal when removed, not when first generated. Relax each edge: if a cheaper path is found, update its frontier cost and parent.AI15
            A* orders by f(n)=g(n)+h(n). Admissibility means 0≤h(n)≤h*(n), the true cheapest remaining cost. Consistency means h(n)≤c(n,n′)+h(n′) on every edge, with h(goal)=0; it implies admissibility on states with goal paths. Consistency makes f nondecreasing along a path.AI18
            DFS follows the deepest pending branch using a LIFO stack or recursion. FILO means the same order as LIFO. With the same children as BFS, a left-first DFS visits S,A,C before B; push rightmost children first to pop the leftmost first.AI14

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — UCS orders by accumulated g rather than h alone.

            B · correct — Greedy best-first selects the node with the smallest heuristic estimate h.

            C · incorrect — DFS follows a LIFO/deepest-branch order rather than minimum h.

            D · incorrect — A* uses g+h, while the stem explicitly uses only h.

            Question 233

            Which of the following best defines a heuristic in the context of AI search?

            • A. A function that estimates how close a state is to the goal
            • B. A guaranteed optimal path to the goal
            • C. A method that always avoids revisiting states
            • D. A brute-force enumeration of all possible states

            Source

            • Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 35

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Check how the method selects its next candidate, what information it uses, and which cost, depth or heuristic assumptions the question supplies.

            Study-guide sections

            AI17 · Heuristics and greedy best-first search

            AI12 · Frontiers and evaluation criteria

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            AI17 · Heuristics and greedy best-first search

            AI12 · Frontiers and evaluation criteria

            Correct answer: A — A problem-specific estimate of remaining cost or promise.

            AI17 defines a heuristic h(n) as estimating remaining cost or evaluating promise. A’s closeness wording captures that estimate rather than an exact path guarantee. A heuristic does not inherently prevent repeated states and is not exhaustive enumeration; those are separate search-policy or bookkeeping choices. Its quality and computation cost affect practical search.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            A heuristic h(n) estimates remaining cost or evaluates promise using problem-specific knowledge. It can reduce explored work, but computing it also costs time. Uninformed algorithms use only the problem definition and known costs; UCS remains uninformed despite using g.AI17
            A search node records a state plus parent, action, depth and path cost. Expanding a node generates its successors. OPEN or frontier stores discovered candidates awaiting expansion; CLOSED records expanded states. Reaching the same state through different paths does not imply the same node or cost.AI12

            Choice by choice

            A · correct — Estimating closeness or remaining cost is the heuristic role defined in AI17.

            B · incorrect — An estimate is not itself a guaranteed optimal path.

            C · incorrect — Repeated-state avoidance requires duplicate handling rather than following from heuristic estimation.

            D · incorrect — Exhaustive enumeration is a search method, not the definition of a heuristic estimate.

            Question 235

            In which of the following Learning methods an agent receives feedback in the form of rewards or penalties to maximize cumulative reward?

            • A. Supervised learning
            • B. Reinforcement learning
            • C. Semi-supervised learning
            • D. Unsupervised learning

            Source

            • Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 83

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Identify the training feedback, prediction target or measured error. Keep learning objectives separate from model architecture and data modality.

            Study-guide sections

            AI33 · Reinforcement learning

            AI31 · Supervised learning and prediction

            AI32 · Unsupervised, semi-supervised and active learning

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            AI33 · Reinforcement learning

            AI31 · Supervised learning and prediction

            AI32 · Unsupervised, semi-supervised and active learning

            Correct answer: B — Reinforcement learning.

            AI33 defines RL through interaction, rewards and improvement of a policy to maximize expected cumulative reward. The reward may be delayed and does not provide a correct-action label. Supervised and semi-supervised learning instead concern target labels, while unsupervised discovery lacks the defining action-reward interaction described here.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            An RL agent observes state information, takes an action, receives reward and a new observation, and improves its policy to maximize expected cumulative reward. Rewards evaluate outcomes rather than supply the correct action label. Rewards may be delayed; not every correct-looking action receives immediate reward.AI33
            Supervised learning fits a mapping from labeled input–target examples. Classification predicts discrete labels, such as institution generations or spam/nonspam; regression predicts numeric quantities, such as prices. Predictive analytics uses historical patterns to forecast outcomes and can use either. Specify the target before choosing a method.AI31
            Semi-supervised learning combines some labels with additional unlabeled data. Active learning chooses informative cases for an oracle to label; it still uses labels. “Exploratory learning” is not an exclusive standard synonym: it can mean unsupervised exploration or active data acquisition, so define the feedback. A task named summarization or time-series analysis is not automatically supervised; its training targets determine that.AI32
            Unsupervised learning seeks structure without target labels: clustering groups similar examples; association finds co-occurrence; dimensionality reduction compresses features. Good clusters have high within-cluster similarity and low between-cluster similarity under an appropriate distance. K-means alternates assignment to nearest centroids and centroid updates.AI32

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Supervised learning fits labeled targets rather than defining behavior through cumulative interaction rewards.

            B · correct — Reward or penalty feedback guiding cumulative-return improvement is the defining RL mechanism.

            C · incorrect — Semi-supervised learning mixes labeled and unlabeled examples, not necessarily action rewards.

            D · incorrect — Unsupervised learning discovers unlabeled structure rather than optimizing an interaction reward policy.
